**Short-term forecast models and typical August rainy-season dynamics in Mexico City point to a daytime maximum near 26–27 °C on 4 August, producing the tight clustering of market-implied odds around those two outcomes.** 

At 2,240 m elevation, the city’s highland location keeps average August highs near 24–26 °C even in the core of the wet season; afternoon convection and cloud build-up frequently cap temperatures by reducing incoming solar radiation and enhancing evaporative cooling. Recent model runs show modest differences in the timing and coverage of showers: earlier or more widespread cloud decks favor the 26 °C outcome, while brief clearing or delayed convection allows brief warming toward 27–28 °C before the usual late-day rain. Urban heat-island effects and weak downslope winds from the surrounding mountains add small positive anomalies, but these are largely offset by the high humidity and frequent precipitation that characterize the current monsoon pattern. With resolution only hours away, traders are weighting the latest high-resolution guidance on cloud fraction and boundary-layer moisture, keeping the implied probabilities for 26 °C and 27 °C nearly even while assigning low odds to extremes outside the 25–28 °C envelope.

Persistent high humidity, trade-wind moisture, and strong afternoon convection typically generate scattered thunderstorms that increase cloud cover and limit peak heating after morning sunshine allows temperatures to climb. Historical August averages near 29–30°C, combined with recent ensemble guidance showing only modest day-to-day variability, explain why 32°C holds the highest market-implied probability. Brief clearer intervals can permit brief spikes to 33°C, while heavier or earlier rain favors 31°C or lower. No significant large-scale anomalies such as unusual sea-surface temperatures or suppressed convection have emerged in the latest model runs, keeping probabilities tightly clustered around these values ahead of the final forecast updates.
